title: Longest Common Subsequence
statement:
Find the length of the longest subsequence that two strings share.

Contract
- `first` and `second` are non-null and may be empty. They may contain any characters.
- A subsequence keeps the original order of characters but may skip some; it need not be
  contiguous.
- Return the length of the longest string that is a subsequence of both inputs, or 0 when they
  share none.

Examples
- `lcsLength("abcde", "ace")` returns `3` ("ace").
- `lcsLength("abc", "xyz")` returns `0`.
- `lcsLength("axbycz", "abc")` returns `3`.
hints: Compare the last characters. If they match they can both be part of the answer; if not, one of them must be dropped.
Let table[i][j] be the answer for the first i and first j characters. A match extends table[i-1][j-1] by one; otherwise take the larger of table[i-1][j] and table[i][j-1].
Each row depends only on the previous row, so two rows are enough. Intended complexity: O(n^2) time and O(n) space, where n is the length of each string.
inputSyntax: Input: the two strings separated by a space, for example: abcde ace
